The newly identified species has ⁣been named Baminornis zhenghensis.Its fossils display a unique combination of features, including birdlike shoulder and pelvic girdles and also a hand structure resembling that of nonavian dinosaurs [3[3[3[3 ].

Critically important Revelation Pushes Back origin of Birds to Late ​Middle⁤ Jurassic Period In November 2023,​ a joint ​team⁢ from the Institute of Vertebrate paleontology and⁤ Paleoanthropology of ‍the​ Chinese Academy of Sciences ​and the Fujian Institute ⁢of Geological Survey made a ‌groundbreaking⁢ revelation​ in‍ Daxi Village, Fujian’s Zhenghe County. They uncovered fossils⁢ of a​ bird from the⁣ late Middle Jurassic period,⁢ approximately 150 million years old. This discovery ⁣rewrites the‍ history of avian evolution and pushes back the⁤ origin of birds to this ancient ‌period.
Interview wiht dr. Min Wang, ‍Specialist in⁣ Avian Paleontology World-Today-News.com (WTN): Dr.Min Wang, thank you for joining us today.‌ Can you tell our readers about‌ the ‍meaning‌ of this ⁢recent fossil discovery?
Dr.Min Wang: The discovery of Baminornis zhenghensis is incredibly significant as ⁤it pushes the origin of birds‌ back to the late Middle Jurassic period. This bird,​ with it’s unique combination of birdlike shoulder and pelvic girdles and dinosaur-like ​hand structure, provides valuable insights into the evolutionary history of birds.
WTN: ⁤What makes Baminornis zhenghensis stand out among other bird fossils?
Dr. Min Wang: Baminornis zhenghensis is ⁣the sole Jurassic and the ⁣oldest short-tailed bird yet discovered. Its features,⁢ which include‌ birdlike shoulder and ⁤pelvic girdles,‌ push ​back‍ the appearance of this derived⁣ bird ⁢feature by nearly 20 million ⁣years. It⁢ looks more like ‍modern birds than Archaeopteryx,highlighting its significance in understanding bird evolution.
WTN: How does⁣ this discovery fit ‌into the broader context of bird evolution?
Dr. Min Wang: birds⁢ evolved from dinosaurs, one of the most astounding chapters in evolutionary history.This process involved significant changes‍ in bones, muscles, and‍ other​ biological structures, representing a ⁢leap from land to sky. The fossils of ​Baminornis⁤ zhenghensis provide a rare glimpse into ⁤this transformative period.
WTN: ​ Can you elaborate ‍on the significance of the Zhenghe Fauna, where the fossils⁣ were found?
dr. min Wang: The zhenghe Fauna ⁣offers a rare glimpse into the ecosystems ⁣of the late ⁤Mesozoic era. it is ​indeed a treasure ​trove‍ for understanding the origins of the variety of⁢ life we see today. The⁤ discovery​ of Baminornis zhenghensis within this⁤ context enhances ⁢our understanding of how birds evolved and adapted over time.
Conclusion The discovery of Baminornis zhenghensis in Daxi Village,​ Fujian’s Zhenghe County, ⁤has ‌pushed ‍back the origin ⁤of ⁣birds to the late Middle Jurassic ​period. This fossil,⁣ with its unique combination of features, rewrites ⁢the history ⁤of avian evolution and ‍provides valuable insights into the transformative‌ period when birds evolved from dinosaurs. The Zhenghe fauna, where the fossils were found, offers a ⁤rare glimpse into the ecosystems of the late Mesozoic era⁢ and is a treasure trove‌ for ‍understanding the origins of ‌the ‍variety of life we see today.
